recommendation: Keep the commit. It completes the remaining semantic part of FHIR-31944 without duplicating the already-correct POST examples or self-link wording maintained elsewhere.
issue_request: FHIR-31944 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core request to make POST search syntax less hand-wavy, show real application/x-www-form-urlencoded body content, state that servers SHALL support body parameters and MAY support URL query parameters, clarify URL/body equivalence and restriction handling, and keep self links expressed with parameters in the URL.
initial_application: No commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-31944 was found. Related R5 work in 7415a1eb0824ba59d977db335205d71eed004312 added modern POST search examples and summary rows, and e441170220c19e992f803667b245e63dcdd508cf moved transport-protocol guidance to source/http.html. Current source already covered body support, URL parameter allowance, and GET-style self links, but not the accepted-parameter equivalence or ignore behavior.
additional_context: FHIR-I September 2021 minutes confirm the intended uniform treatment of parameters split between URL and body. FHIR-31943 supplies the companion GET/POST method-support context, FHIR-33220 later makes the self-link rule explicit, FHIR-38744 was retracted and does not weaken the body-parameter SHALL, and FHIR-51506 is consistent with self links reflecting actual search parameters.
reconciliation: Updated source/http.html in the REST (HTTP) search section to state that accepted POST URL and body parameters have no semantic difference and are combined into a single search parameter set. Expanded the existing URL-parameter restriction paragraph to say unsupported POST URL parameters may be rejected or ignored, with the self link reflecting the parameters actually used.
source_changes: source/http.html: added POST URL/body parameter equivalence wording after the mixed URL/body POST example.
source/http.html: expanded URL query-parameter restriction guidance to allow reject-or-ignore handling and point to the self link for parameters actually used.

related_jiras.note: Companion Published issue about GET/POST search support and 405 behavior; it explains the method-security context but was not decided here.
Later Published issue making POST-search self links always GET-style URLs; current source/search.html already covers that rule.
Published issue whose application added the current POST search examples and summary rows.
Published refactor moved transport-protocol guidance from the Search page to the HTTP page, leaving this narrow semantic gap.
Retracted no-change issue confirms the POST body-parameter SHALL should not be weakened.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive with Modification issue asking for clearer POST search examples and explicit rules for POST body parameters, URL parameters, URL/body equivalence, restrictions, and self links.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes the final WG request and the source behavior that must be checked.

evidence_items.summary: FHIR-I minutes record the FHIR-31944 motion and state that servers SHALL support body parameters, MAY support URL parameters, MAY set URL-parameter rules, and SHALL treat split URL/body parameters uniformly.
evidence_items.learned: The meeting record confirms the Jira resolution and the exact uniform-treatment semantics.

evidence_items.summary: The active REST (HTTP) page now documents POST body support, optional URL query parameters, accepted URL/body parameter equivalence, and reject-or-ignore handling for unsupported POST URL parameters.
evidence_items.learned: The source change is in build scope and addresses the remaining FHIR-31944 semantic gap.

evidence_items.summary: The Search page already says self links SHALL be expressed as HTTP GET-based searches with relevant parameters as query parameters and may not be resolvable.
evidence_items.learned: The self-link portion of FHIR-31944 is already correctly represented, so no duplicate edit is needed.

evidence_items.summary: Related R5 commits added the modern POST search examples and summary rows, then moved search transport-protocol guidance from source/search.html to source/http.html.
evidence_items.learned: Historical related work explains why most of the issue was already applied and why the remaining gap is isolated to HTTP-page semantics.

evidence_items.summary: A 2018 implementer thread asked how to handle POST search parameters split across query string and form body, with responses discussing accepting all, errors, self-link disclosure, and treating repeated parameters uniformly.
evidence_items.learned: The community thread shows the ambiguity that FHIR-31944 later resolved and supports adding explicit current-source guidance.
